investigacion.base:
**Current count: 6 different winners** (as of about Oct 12–14, 2026). The total can't go down. Whether it ends at 6 depends mostly on whether Piastri, Hadjar or someone else wins one of the last races.

**Resolution source (ESPN, updated about 9 days ago, ~Oct 5):** ESPN says Mercedes has been the dominant force throughout with Italian youngster Kimi Antonelli leading the drivers' championship. Its latest listed race is Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia (Round 16) — Winner: Max Verstappen (Red Bull). That's the relocated Bahrain race, held Oct 4. ESPN may not include the newest round yet.

**Winners so far:**
- **Kimi Antonelli: 8 wins.** China, Japan, Miami, Canada, Monaco, Belgium, Italy, Spain.
- **George Russell: 3 wins.** Australia, Austria, Azerbaijan.
- **Lando Norris: 2 wins.** Hungary, Netherlands.
- **Lewis Hamilton: 1 win.** Barcelona.
- **Charles Leclerc: 1 win.** Britain.
- **Max Verstappen: 1–2 wins.** Malaysia-hosted Bahrain GP, plus probably Singapore.

Sources: whenstherace.com, statsniper.

**Possible newest round:** F1-fansite (2 days ago) says the season has 23 Grand Prix rounds, of which 17 have been completed so far, and that Max Verstappen won the most recent Grand Prix at Marina Bay Street Circuit. That would be Round 17, probably Oct 11. I haven't confirmed it with a second source, but either way Verstappen is already counted, so the total stays at 6.

**Races left:** About 6 rounds. Based on the usual calendar these are probably the US (Austin), Mexico, Brazil, Las Vegas, Qatar and Abu Dhabi, ending in early December. I haven't checked these dates.

**Who could still add a 7th winner:**
- **Oscar Piastri** is the most likely. He's in a race-winning McLaren and has finished on the podium this year (2nd in Japan).
- **Isack Hadjar** (Red Bull) has finished as high as 4th and 5th.
- **Pierre Gasly** (Alpine) has a 3rd place, in Monaco.
- Others would need chaos races.

**Base rates for distinct winners per season:** 2021: 5; 2022: 5; 2023: 2; 2024: 7; 2025: 4 (Verstappen, Norris, Piastri, Russell). So 2026 is already at the high end of recent seasons. Since 2024's 7 winners, getting a new first-time winner of the season in the last 6 races has been fairly uncommon.

**Prediction markets:** I didn't find any market prices.

**Status quo:** If nobody new wins, the question resolves as **6**. A first win of the season for Piastri (or another driver) would make it 7 or more.

**Sources:**

- [2](https://whenstherace.com/results/)

- [4](https://www.f1-fansite.com/f1-results/f1-standings-2026-championship/)

criterios: This question will resolve as the number of different drivers who win at least one Grand Prix in 2026 FIA Formula One World Championship.

(a) **Time left:** About 6 races remain, ending in early December 2026. The answer will be known in roughly 7 weeks.

(b) **Status quo:** Six different drivers have already won: Antonelli, Russell, Norris, Hamilton, Leclerc and Verstappen. The count cannot go down, so if no new driver wins, the answer is 6.

(c) **Base rates:**
- Recent seasons produced 5, 5, 2, 7 and 4 distinct winners, so 6 already sits at the high end.
- A new winner of the season appearing in the final third of a year is uncommon but does happen, especially when several cars can win.
- Piastri has a competitive McLaren. Norris has won twice in it, but Piastri has gone 17 races without a win.
- With about 6 races left, I put roughly 20–25% on Piastri winning at least once.
- I add about 8–10% for someone else winning a chaotic race (Hadjar, Gasly, Sainz, Albon and others), or for a sprint/Grand Prix ambiguity.

(d) **Unexpected scenario:** Piastri wins a race in Austin or Brazil, and then a wet or chaotic race such as Brazil or Las Vegas hands Hadjar or Gasly a victory, giving 8. The answer could also be 5 if the research has miscounted, for example by counting the Barcelona race when it was not a championship Grand Prix. That is unlikely.
